title: Bram and the Landfall
premise: Mirabel Iversen is hired to resupply a survey expedition that has gone silent deep in the unmapped headwaters of the Vessel River. She finds the camp intact but the scientists changed—carrying fragments of a drowned city whose ruins rewrite the memories of anyone who lingers, including her own. As the river rises toward an early landfall flood and the expedition's sponsor moves to seize the site, Mirabel must choose between recovering what she has lost of herself and destroying the only proof she ever existed as she was. She scuttles the ruins beneath the floodwater, keeps one stolen memory as her own secret, and brings home a crew who no longer remember why they went.
about_author: C. M. Kavanagh is the pen name of a former deckhand turned novelist who spent six seasons working inland waterways before trading the wheelhouse for a writing desk. Their fiction blends river lore, quiet dread, and characters who trust the current more than they trust people.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A routine charter upriver turns strange when the survey team's scheduled radio check fails for the third day, and the expedition's cold-eyed sponsor, Aldous Wren, offers her triple pay to run supplies regardless. She takes the contract against her instincts. Emotional beat: unease disguised as professionalism—the reader feels the trap closing before she does.

chapters.title: The Mood of the Water
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Loading the Bram, she notices Wren's crew smuggling in sealed crates marked with survey coordinates far beyond any legal claim. Her old deckhand, Sef, warns her the headwaters have swallowed better boats than hers. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by greed; Mirabel commits to the journey knowing the cargo doesn't add up.

chapters.title: Past the Last Chart
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The river narrows into uncharted water; sandbars shift where maps say open channel, as if the river itself is rearranging to keep something hidden. They find the first abandoned supply cache ransacked from the inside. Emotional beat: isolation deepens—the wilderness stops feeling indifferent and starts feeling deliberate.

chapters.title: The Camp That Waits
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She reaches the survey camp at dusk: tents standing, instruments running, but the five scientists sitting motionless around a cold fire, alive and wrong. Team lead Dr. Halloway greets her by a name that isn't hers—and it fits. Emotional beat: uncanny dread; the horror is quiet, polite, and patient.

chapters.title: What the Stone Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Mirabel and Halloway's recovered journal entries. Below the bluff lies a submerged ruin whose carved stones imprint memories—some belonging to people centuries dead. Halloway confesses the team can no longer tell which recollections are their own. Emotional beat: grief for a self you can feel slipping away.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Wren arrives by floatplane with armed contractors, revealing he always knew what the stones do—he wants them weaponized or sold. He orders the site stripped before the seasonal landfall flood seals the gorge. Mirabel realizes her memory of her daughter's face now contains details she never lived. Emotional beat: fury fused with vertigo; power revealed as theft of other minds.

chapters.title: The Rising
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Rain swells the river days ahead of schedule; the contractors' barge grounds on a bar that wasn't there yesterday. Sef defects to Mirabel's side, and two scientists beg to be evacuated even without their memories. Emotional beat: desperation sharpening into resolve—the flood becomes both deadline and ally.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, climax. In the storm surge she runs the Bram through the collapsing gorge while Wren's men try to haul the core stones aboard. She deliberately breaches the ruin's retaining wall, letting the flood bury the site—and Wren's ambition—with it. Wren drowns reaching for a stone instead of a rope. Emotional beat: cathartic sacrifice; she chooses oblivion over ownership.

chapters.title: Passengers Without Luggage
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Running downriver with the survivors, she discovers none of them—including her—can fully account for the voyage. Halloway asks what they found; Mirabel hears herself say 'nothing worth the trip.' Only she knows she kept one stone fragment hidden in the bilge. Emotional beat: hollowed-out tenderness; survival with a hole shaped like truth.

chapters.title: The Sandbar's Mood
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, resolution. Weeks later, back on familiar water, Mirabel reads the river's moods as always—but sometimes she knows a channel's turn before she sees it, knowledge that isn't hers. She weighs the fragment in the bilge and finally drops it overboard at the exact sandbar where the river first lied to her. Emotional beat: hard-won peace; identity reclaimed not as certainty but as choice.
